licence_detail: CC BY-NC 4.0 (challenge.isic-archive.com/data lists ISIC 2019 as CC-BY-NC; HF flwrlabs card cc-by-nc-4.0). Aggregates BCN_20000, HAM10000 and MSK, each to be cited. No registration. Note: the BCN_20000 half is separately on figshare 24140028 under CC BY 4.0 (that is the permissive 'bcn20000' row).
worthwhile: yes (MMBU source, 91 public rows, largest accessible NC source); image-level redundancy with permissive set is high

download.registry_route: hf flwrlabs/fed-isic2019: works but 224x224 center-cropped/downsampled, 23,247 of 25,331 images, no image ids
download.tested_route: direct https://isic-archive.s3.amazonaws.com/challenges/2019/ISIC_2019_Training_Input.zip (9.8 GB, zip-range sampling, 140 files = 56 MB): works, full-res

image_findings: Registry route: 6/6 are dermoscopy lesion crops but 224x224 and visibly centre-cropped (lesion often cut off). S3 route: 6/6 are dermoscopy at original aspect (BCN-style 1024x1024 squares, HAM 600x450 rectangles, MSK '_downsampled' with ruler/vignette), resized to 512 long side. 12 (HF route) and 8 (S3 route) of the files examined were dropped as near-duplicates of mmbu-public.
label_findings: All six fields registry-supplied and correct: optical imaging / dermoscopy / skin / human / dermatology+oncology; stain masked. No conflicts. MMBU public dermoscopy rows (117) carry domain dermatology only, so 'oncology' is an extra multi value (same in every permissive dermoscopy set; harmless).
metadata_findings: Registry route columns hf:split, hf:center, hf:label (0-7 class index) are not Pass-2 fields; none trusted. S3 route has no metadata in the zip (ground-truth CSV is a separate file, diagnosis only). Overlap measured from the S3 zip listings: ISIC 2019 contains all 10,015 ISIC 2018 Task 3 images and 2,593 of 2,594 ISIC 2018 Task 1 images; ISIC 2017 (CC0, permissive isic-2017) is 1,800/2,000 inside 2018 Task 1 and therefore inside 2019.
fixes: route: isic-2019 -> direct S3 zip (full resolution)

licence_detail: Split licence on challenge.isic-archive.com/data: Tasks 1-2 images CC-0; Task 3 (HAM10000/MSK) CC-BY-NC. The registry route (MedOtter/ISIC2018: image+mask, 2,594/100/1,000 rows) is Task 1, i.e. the CC-0 part; the HF card states no licence. Registry 'multiple' is therefore not nc for this route.

download.registry_route: hf MedOtter/ISIC2018: state error 'ArrowInvalid: offset overflow while concatenating arrays' after ~13 min and ~14 GB RSS (HF streaming shuffle buffer of 2,000 full-size images, see bug B1)
download.tested_route: direct ISIC2018_Task1-2_Training_Input.zip (11.2 GB, zip-range, 140 files = 690 MB): works

image_findings: 6/6 dermoscopy (some with ruler, round vignette), correct. 512 px long side.
label_findings: Registry-supplied labels correct (optical imaging / dermoscopy / skin / human / dermatology+oncology).
metadata_findings: Only path:d1 = zip folder name, not trusted. Duplication measured from zip listings: Task 1 images are 100% inside ISIC 2019 (2,593/2,594), 1,800/2,000 of ISIC 2017 train and 806/900 of ISIC 2016 train are inside it (permissive isic-2016/isic-2017, CC0), and permissive medsegmnist-derm2d is ISIC 2018 Task 1 by its own title. Its 13 public rows are explained by those too.
fixes: drop (redundant: superset of nothing new; Task 1 is CC-0 and already in permissive isic-2016/2017/medsegmnist-derm2d, and 100% inside isic-2019)

licence_detail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 per arXiv 2406.16039v2 (dataset paper); GitHub code repo is Apache-2.0 (code only). Hosted on Synapse (syn60239970 / DOI 10.7303/syn64891826.1); Synapse REST shows no access requirement on the project but anonymous download is refused ('Anonymous users have only READ access permission'): a Synapse login/token is needed. Underlying videos are Cholec80/CholecT50 (themselves CC BY-NC-SA).
worthwhile: would be (89 public rows, 41.9k frames) but only after a manual Synapse download

download.issue: DOI resolves to www.synapse.org, an unsupported host in download.py; file entity syn66477541 (cholecinstanceseg.zip) + syn66477699 (metadata csv) need an authenticated Synapse download; no pixels could be inspected

image_findings: Not inspected (blocked). Per paper: 854x480 frames (three sequences 1920x1080) from 85 cholecystectomies, same appearance as CholecSeg8k (Cholec80).
label_findings: Registry labels (endoscopy / laparoscopy / abdomen,gallbladder,liver candidates / human / gastroenterology+surgery) look right for the described frames; not testable here.
metadata_findings: cholecinstanceseg_metadata.csv links annotation files to source datasets and tool presence; video id VID-xx; none of it is a Pass-2 field.
fixes: manual: download cholecinstanceseg.zip from Synapse into data/raw/cholecinstanceseg/archives/ with a Synapse token (needs the user); optional route method manual

licence_detail: Authoritative record (UCL RDR = figshare article 26531686, API) says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, matching the registry. The Hugging Face mirror drdreets/PitVis-2023 says cc-by-nc-nd-4.0 and is gated (auto), which is why the registry route ends in 'manual'. Use the figshare route; if ND were applied (frame extraction/resizing = adaptation) the dataset would be unusable.
worthwhile: yes: the only substantial endoscopic head-and-neck source; 36 public rows, no permissive counterpart

download.tested_route: figshare 26531686: 25 mp4 (0.86-3.3 GB each, 42.8 GB) + annotation csvs; with --max-gb 2 only 2 videos fit (1.79 GB) -> 8 frames

image_findings: 6/6 correct endoscopic transsphenoidal pituitary surgery frames (circular endoscope view, blood, bone, instruments). One of the six frames is a blocky, heavily upscaled low-resolution frame (video start/keyframe artefact). 8/16 candidate frames were near-duplicates of mmbu-public. Only 2 videos sampled, so this is a weak sample; full run draws 8 frames per video from 25 videos.
label_findings: Registry: endoscopy / white-light endoscopy / human correct. body_part candidates [head, nose, pituitary gland] omit 'head and neck', which is what MMBU uses for all 36 public PitVis rows (all 36 are body_part=head and neck, domain=otolaryngology+surgery); registry domain endocrinology+neurology+surgery lacks otolaryngology. Fix proposed below (note: derived from eval-set label conventions, flag if the team does not want that).
metadata_findings: Annotation CSVs (surgical step / instrument ids) are not Pass-2 fields; no trusted columns.
fixes: labels: body_part candidates [head and neck, nose, pituitary gland]; domain multi [endocrinology, neurology, otolaryngology, surgery]

licence_detail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (GitHub soroushj/mhsma-dataset; LICENSE file shipped inside the Kaggle copy is the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 text). 235 male-infertility patients. No registration.
worthwhile: yes if fixed: 68 public rows (2.2% of mmbu-public), the best rows-per-image ratio in the layer; all public sperm rows are brightfield microscopy / light microscopy
image_findings: ALL 22 pilot 'images' are garbage: 6/6 inspected are tall 1xN grey strips (66x512, 33x512, 64x240, 128x300...), because prepare.read_array slices a (1000,128,128) stack along its smallest axis (width) and tiles the label vectors too (bug B4). Reading the arrays correctly (axis 0) gives real 128x128 (and a duplicate 64x64 copy of the same 1,540 cells) greyscale unstained live-sperm crops (head and tail visible), 6/6 plausible, blurry, low resolution.
label_findings: Registry labels light microscopy / brightfield microscopy / sperm cells / human / andrology are consistent with MMBU's own convention for sperm images (93 public sperm rows: all brightfield microscopy, stain none). Stain masked. Unstained label-free images could equally be argued to be phase/DIC contrast, but MMBU says brightfield.
metadata_findings: mhsma.csv is a file listing (name, size), not per-sample metadata; the y_{acrosome,head,vacuole,tail}_*.npy 0/1 morphology flags are not Pass-2 fields. Nothing trusted.
fixes: fix src (prepare.read_array: treat 3-D uint8 arrays with equal last two dims as image stacks along axis 0; skip 1-D arrays)
exclude_paths: x_64_ (duplicate low-res copy) and y_ (label vectors)

licence_detail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (HF minwoosun/CholecSeg8k card; Kaggle newslab/cholecseg8k; arXiv 2012.12453). Frames derived from Cholec80 (CC BY-NC-SA). No registration.
worthwhile: yes, modestly: 18 public rows, accessible stand-in for the Cholec80 appearance while cholecinstanceseg is blocked

download.strategy: hf-files:zip-range (HF streaming failed with RuntimeError, fell back to file listing)

image_findings: 6/6 correct laparoscopic cholecystectomy frames (gallbladder, liver, hook/grasper), black circular border, 512x288. 73/140 sampled frames (52%) are near-duplicates of mmbu-public images and were dropped, so the usable yield per file is about half.
label_findings: endoscopy / laparoscopy / human correct (path:d1 trusted for submodality, agrees). body_part candidates [abdomen, gallbladder, liver] is right in substance (MMBU's own laparoscopy rows are 83% 'abdomen', gallbladder 0, liver 2). Domain gastroenterology+surgery vs MMBU laparoscopy rows 'surgery' (355/405).
metadata_findings: Folder names videoNN/videoNN_FFFFF are not Pass-2 fields; masks (_endo_mask, watermask, color_mask) are correctly skipped by files.py.

licence_detail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (Warwick TIA page; HF RationAI/PanNuke card). Warwick page adds: for academic research, must cite the PanNuke papers. 3 folds, 7,901 patches. No registration.
worthwhile: marginal: 12 public rows; the only NC dataset with per-image organ labels at 40x H&E (19 tissue types)
image_findings: 6/6 are 256x256 H&E patches at 40x (nuclei-level crops, no tissue context), correct for H&E. Small, no JPEG artefacts. Many patches are pure nuclei/stroma texture where 'whole slide imaging' is a stretch, but it is the same convention used for NCT-CRC-HE and BRACS.
label_findings: modality light microscopy / submodality whole slide imaging / stain h&e / human / oncology+pathology: correct. body_part is registry-masked although hf:tissue (ClassLabel 0-18: Adrenal Gland, Bile Duct, Bladder, Breast, Cervix, Colon, Esophagus, Head & Neck, Kidney, Liver, Lung, Ovarian, Pancreatic, Prostate, Skin, Stomach, Testis, Thyroid, Uterus) gives it per image. With the 16 override rows below AND the int-to-str fix (bug B3) body_part becomes hard for 83/100 images (adrenal gland, bile duct, testis have no class).
metadata_findings: hf:split (fold1-3, not a Pass-2 field) and hf:tissue (integer index; review.csv lists the integers unmapped). Verified in scratch: overrides alone do nothing (column is 'trusted' but values are ints and never match), with a str() cast in apply the overrides take effect.

licence_detail: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (BBBC041 page: 'images and ground truth licensed by Jane Hung'; cite 'image set BBBC041v1' + Ljosa 2012). Kaggle copy kmader/malaria-bounding-boxes. No registration.
worthwhile: low: 7 public rows; Giemsa blood smears are covered by 7 permissive datasets (lacuna-malaria, raabin-wbc, ...)

download.strategy: per-file Kaggle (2,661 listed files, 6.8 GB listed)
download.issue: 57/140 sampled files unreadable (bug B2: Kaggle returns a zip wrapper for files over ~1 MB and get_file stores it under the .png name); the Kaggle record also contains every image twice (malaria/images and malaria/malaria/images, 1,328 unique images) plus a whole-dataset zip

image_findings: 6/6 correct: Giemsa-stained P. vivax thin blood smears (trophozoites, gametocytes, leukocytes), 1600x1200 -> 512x384, varied staining/colour casts, one blurry/thick region. Lost 57/140 to the zip wrapper, which biases the sample to smaller PNGs.
label_findings: light microscopy / brightfield microscopy / blood / giemsa correct. specimen candidates [human, plasmodium] fine (MMBU's Giemsa-brightfield public rows: 32 human, 4 'p. falciparum-infected red blood cells').
metadata_findings: No trusted columns (path folder names 'malaria'); training.json/test.json carry per-cell boxes and classes (red blood cell, trophozoite, schizont, gametocyte, leukocyte) which are not Pass-2 fields.
fixes: exclude_paths: ^malaria/malaria/ (duplicate copy), only if the dataset is kept

licence_detail: Repository (github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k): CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. The images belong to two dermatology atlases (Atlas Dermatologico, DermaAmin); the repo ships URLs only and says many are broken. The HF mirror ZYXue/Fitzpatrick_17k carries no licence tag and redistributes the pixels (as a VQA reformatting), so the atlas rights are not covered by the CC licence.
worthwhile: no: 10 public rows; 16 permissive clinical-photography datasets (24.7k images) incl. SCIN already planned; legal exposure on image rights
image_findings: 6/6 correct clinical skin photographs (hand, knee, back, scalp, leg, areola) with a corner watermark ('SFS') on several; variable 400-500 px resolution. 8 near-duplicates of mmbu-public and 7 in-dataset duplicates among the files examined, the latter because the HF copy has one row per question, not per image.
label_findings: clinical photography / skin / human / dermatology correct. Fitzpatrick skin type labels and the three/nine-partition disease labels are not Pass-2 fields.
metadata_findings: Columns are the VQA reformatting (pure_question, answer, choices, is_correct_prompt, question): none maps to a Pass-2 field, none trusted, review.csv empty.

licence_detail: CC BY-NC 3.0 (Mendeley Data c7fjbxcgj9 v4, public-api data_licence 'CC BY NC 3.0'); not NC-SA. Single 504 MB zip. No registration.
worthwhile: no: 6 public rows; same lineage as permissive edd2020 (CC-BY-4.0, 43 public rows, same select group) and 24 permissive white-light endoscopy datasets

download.state: manual in the stock run (Mendeley listing returns HTTP 403 to python-requests, bug B5); the zip downloads fine with curl from the public API (302 to S3). I fetched it by hand into raw/ead2020/archives and ran the harness (manual-drop).
download.issue: first harness run crashed in metalabel.load_tables: TypeError: Cannot perform reduction 'mean' with string dtype (pandas-3 variant of V5 bug B1, listed here as B6); validated through a scratch wrapper

image_findings: 6/6 are GI endoscopy frames (oesophagus/stomach/colon-like lumen), octagonal mask, artefacts (specular, bubbles, blood); one frame is an endoscope screen grab with a patient-data text panel (age/DOB/physician): minor PHI-style burn-in. 5,606 media files in the zip: frames, allDetection bbox images (same frames as 'frames'), segmentation set and Phase-II sequences, so among the 150 candidates examined 27 were in-dataset duplicates and 23 near-duplicates of mmbu-public were dropped.
label_findings: endoscopy / white-light endoscopy / human correct; body_part candidates [bladder, colon, esophagus, stomach] reasonable (sources are mixed GI and urological endoscopy); domain gastroenterology+urology ok. No metadata distinguishes organ per image.
metadata_findings: Only path columns (EAD2020_dataType_framesOnly, allDetection_training, bbox_images, frames, ...): none trusted. Bounding-box XML/txt labels are artefact classes, not Pass-2 fields.

licence_detail: CC BY-NC 4.0 (Zenodo 15088516 API: cc-by-nc-4.0, open access). 16.9 GB in 14 files.
worthwhile: no: 0 public rows; OCTA submodality already has 8,037 planned permissive images (target 8,000); only unique aspect is skin OCTA

download.issue: stock route picks the 5 GB 'Contrast - 3D.zip' first (331 volumes of 90x483x512 uint8, 22 MB each); with --max-gb 2 the zip-range sampler downloaded ~2.8 GB on disk over >45 min before I aborted it. The record holds 5 filter variants (Contrast, Norm, Frangi, Morph_angio, Proj_art) of the same 331 scans, 2D and 3D, plus manual segmentations and a 2 GB code zip. With exclude_paths '3D|Contrast|Frangi|Morph_angio|Proj_art|codes|Manual' only 'Norm - 2D.zip' (581 MB, 993 PNG) is used: fast and clean.

image_findings: 6/6 are en-face skin OCTA vessel maps (all/sup/deep projections of the same scans), 6x6-type grey images with vertical motion stripes; correct for OCTA but at first glance indistinguishable from retinal OCTA (the permissive datasets).
label_findings: optical imaging / optical coherence tomography angiography / skin / human / dermatology: correct.
metadata_findings: path:d1 = filter-variant name, path:d2 'TEST from different pathologies' (57 of 993) are not Pass-2 fields; none trusted. Effective unique content is 331 scans x 3 projections, not the registry's 19,800.

licence_detail: CC BY-NC 4.0 (Zenodo 15105761 API cc-by-nc-4.0, open). 2.8 MB + 92.8 MB zips.
worthwhile: no: 71 images from 10 patients; retinal OCTA is covered by 3 permissive datasets (8k images), 0 public rows
image_findings: 6/6 correct en-face superficial-capillary OCTA 6x6 mm, 320x320, Topcon Triton; some with motion artefacts/black bands (expected).
label_findings: optical imaging / optical coherence tomography angiography / eye / human / ophthalmology correct (path:d2 'left eye'/'right eye' trusted for body_part, agrees).
metadata_findings: path:d1 patient id, path:d2 eye: only the second is a Pass-2 field and it agrees with the registry.

licence_detail: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (HF card and LICENSE file; repo Ahus-AIM/EchoXFlow). Open, 666 exam tars, 441 GB total.
worthwhile: no for this pipeline: needs a custom zarr reader; the colour-Doppler data are raw arrays, not displayable images

download.issue: HF streaming found no image column, fell back to whole tar files; prepare found no media ('no images prepared'). Each exam tar holds zarr v2 stores (data/2d_brightness_mode, data/ecg, timestamps/*), blosc-zstd compressed, no png/mp4.

image_findings: Inspected one 28 MB exam by hand (scratch, zarr+numcodecs): 2d_brightness_mode arrays (144x718x242 uint8) are real cardiac B-mode frames but in beamspace (rectangular, not scan-converted: the sector is stretched into a rectangle), which looks unlike the fan-shaped echo images in MMBU or permissive sets. Colour-Doppler channels are raw velocity/power arrays that would need EchoXFlow's own rendering.
label_findings: registry: ultrasound imaging / candidates [3d ultrasound, b-mode ultrasound, color doppler] / heart / cardiology: modality and body part right; submodality would need to be per-recording (the zarr keys 2d_brightness_mode vs doppler arrays carry it), not available to metalabel.
metadata_findings: splits.csv + croissant.json (202 MB) only describe exams/recordings; no trusted columns possible without a zarr reader.
fixes: drop (no reader; beamspace; would need scan conversion)

licence_detail: CC BY NC 3.0 (Mendeley Data fdnb2kyz4f v1, public-api data_licence 'CC BY NC 3.0'; Maltsev, Burnasheva, Chhablani, Kulikov 2019).
worthwhile: no: the record contains no images

download.state: manual (Mendeley HTTP 403 to python-requests, bug B5); checked by hand with curl: the public API lists exactly one file, 'Participants characteristics.xlsx' (11,581 bytes, 48 rows of patient/age/gender/eye/nevus), dataset size 11,581 bytes, no folders
download.issue: registry already shows file_formats [] and effective_images -1

image_findings: No pixels exist in the record (the 3,000 planned images do not exist).
label_findings: n/a. Registry candidates [fundus photography, near-infrared imaging, optical coherence tomography] would have been unusable anyway (three modalities mixed in one pool, per-image modality unknown).
metadata_findings: Participant table: patient code, age, gender, eye, nevus positive/negative; no image names.
